\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پاسگاه} (pâsgâh)}{پاسگاه (pâsgâh)}]{\fa{پاسگاه} (pâsgâh) — a police post; a guard post}

\label{lesson:FA-C453-pasgah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a payment slip, then the Persian for tax.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پاسگاه}}
\textbf{\fa{پاسگاه}} (\emph{pâsgâh}) — \textquotedblleft{}a police post; a guard post\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{جاده} \fa{یک} \fa{پاسگاه} \fa{پلیس} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar jâdde yek pâsgâh-e polis bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was a police post on the road.
\end{quote}

\emph{pâs} 'watch, guard' + \emph{gâh} 'place'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pâsgâh} is a native compound of \emph{pâs} 'watch, guard', the word behind \emph{pâsbân} 'guard', and \emph{gâh} 'place'. EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pâsgâh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pâsgâh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{pâsgâh}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a payment slip, then the Persian for tax, then say \emph{pâsgâh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گمشده} (gomshode)}{گمشده (gomshode)}]{\fa{گمشده} (gomshode) — lost, missing}

\label{lesson:FA-C453-gomshode}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for tax, then the Persian for a police post.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گمشده}}
\textbf{\fa{گمشده}} (\emph{gomshode}) — \textquotedblleft{}lost, missing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کیف} \fa{گمشده} \fa{من} \fa{را} \fa{در} \fa{تاکسی} \fa{پیدا} \fa{کردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Kif-e gomshode-ye man râ dar tâksi peydâ kardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They found my lost bag in the taxi.
\end{quote}

\emph{Ashyâ-ye gomshode} — lost property.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gomshode} is built from native \emph{gom} 'lost', which EtymDB lists, and \emph{shode}, the past participle of \emph{shodan} 'to become'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gomshode}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{gomshode}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for tax, then the Persian for a police post, then say \emph{gomshode} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کیف} \fa{پول} (kif-e pul)}{کیف پول (kif-e pul)}]{\fa{کیف} \fa{پول} (kif-e pul) — a wallet, a purse}

\label{lesson:FA-C453-kif-e-pul}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a police post, then the Persian for lost.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کیف} \fa{پول}}
\textbf{\fa{کیف} \fa{پول}} (\emph{kif-e pul}) — \textquotedblleft{}a wallet, a purse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کیف} \fa{پولم} \fa{را} \fa{در} \fa{اتوبوس} \fa{گم} \fa{کردم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Kif-e pulam râ dar otobus gom kardam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I lost my wallet on the bus.
\end{quote}

\emph{kif} 'bag' + \emph{pul} 'money'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kif-e pul} is built from \emph{kif} 'bag', whose origin is not settled, and \emph{pul} 'money', which EtymDB glosses 'change, small money'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پلیس} \fa{راه} (polis-e râh)}{پلیس راه (polis-e râh)}]{\fa{پلیس} \fa{راه} (polis-e râh) — the traffic police, the highway police}

\label{lesson:FA-C453-polis-e-rah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for lost, then the Persian for a wallet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پلیس} \fa{راه}}
\textbf{\fa{پلیس} \fa{راه}} (\emph{polis-e râh}) — \textquotedblleft{}the traffic police, the highway police\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پلیس} \fa{راه} \fa{ماشین} \fa{ما} \fa{را} \fa{نگه} \fa{داشت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Polis-e râh mâshin-e mâ râ negah dâsht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The highway police stopped our car.
\end{quote}

Inside towns the traffic police is \emph{polis-e râhnamâyi va rânandegi}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{polis-e râh} is built from \emph{polis}, a loan usually traced to French \emph{police}, and native \emph{râh} 'road', from Middle Persian \emph{rāh} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{polis-e râh}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for lost, then the Persian for a wallet, then say \emph{polis-e râh} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شماره} \fa{گرفتن} (shomâre gereftan)}{شماره گرفتن (shomâre gereftan)}]{\fa{شماره} \fa{گرفتن} (shomâre gereftan) — to ring a number, to dial}

\label{lesson:FA-C453-shomare-gereftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a wallet, then the Persian for the traffic police.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شماره} \fa{گرفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{شماره} \fa{گرفتن}} (\emph{shomâre gereftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to ring a number, to dial\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{شماره} \fa{پلیس} \fa{را} \fa{گرفتم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Shomâre-ye polis râ gereftam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I dialled the police number.
\end{quote}

\emph{shomâre} 'number' + \emph{gereftan} 'to take'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{shomâre gereftan} is built from \emph{shomâre} 'number', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{ōšmārag} 'reckoning' (EtymDB), and the native verb \emph{gereftan} 'to take'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
